steps.name: open general
afterLabels: Today's tasks, quadrants, habits and focus — four cards you can keep on your home screen.
Today's tasks · Quadrants · Today's habits · Today's focus
Touch and hold an empty spot on the home screen until the icons jiggle
Tap the “+” in the top-left corner
Search for “Heyta” and pick a size
The system does not let an app place a widget for you, so you add it once by hand.
If the card says “Open Heyta to show your widget” after adding it, opening Heyta once fills it in.
Credentials are kept in memory only and must be re-entered after the app fully exits.
This device remembers your choice, and it still applies after you reopen the app. Your home-screen widgets read the same preference.
Complaints and reports, Opens your mail app with a message to our intake mailbox

steps.name: open export screen
steps.target: Backup & migration, Export a backup, restore data, or import from TickTick
beforeLabels: Trash, Restore the tasks, notes, lists and habits you deleted
Backup & migration, Export a backup, restore data, or import from TickTick
afterLabels: Export, restore, or migrate data on this device. Export runs locally and never touches a server.
Every entity, the complete operation log, and deleted records included. Machine-readable, good for backup or migration.
A task list a person can open and read. It leaves out deleted records and the operation log.
Restore works only into an empty library: it is rejected when this device already has data — nothing existing is cleared or overwritten.
The export is handed to the system share sheet, where you choose where it goes.
The JSON export can be imported back (empty databases only for now); the task list is for reading, not for restoring.
